title: AvatarHub — Images Only
objective: The avatar uploader only accepts image files — checked by extension. Get an executable-looking script file accepted and stored anyway.

verifier.condition: A file whose effective extension, as the storage step actually uses it, is not one of the allowed image extensions is accepted and stored.

weakness: The extension check looks only at whether an allowed image extension appears anywhere in the filename, not at what the file's real, final extension is, so a crafted double extension satisfies the check while actually storing a different file type.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /avatar/upload (filename field; extension matched with .includes() rather than checking the true suffix)
seededData: A simulated uploads directory (never real disk). No pre-existing files.
hints: Upload a real .png and a real .txt first and see how each is handled.
The filter is checking for the presence of an allowed extension, not necessarily what the file actually ends with.
A filename can contain more than one dot.
burpNotes: Upload with a filename like 'shell.php.png' or 'shell.png.php' in Repeater and see which combinations the server accepts, and what it actually stores the file as.
